target_customer: Clinical trial sponsors (Phase II and III, starting with oncology and rare disease) and their data and biometrics teams
problem: Converting raw trial data into SDTM and ADaM datasets, TFLs and submission ready packages takes months of manual programming and data management.
business_model: enterprise software deployed in the sponsor's environment with forward deployed engineers and expert review of outputs (pricing not published)
product_category: AI for clinical trial biometrics and statistical programming

founders.name: Joshua Wang
education: Stanford, studied CS and Math, dropped out
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: USAMO qualifier, USACO Platinum, built multi-agent AI and clinical data automation workflows.

founders.name: Sanmay Sarada
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: built clinical and hospital data infrastructure across diagnostic software systems; employers not named.

technical_complexity.rationale: Output must meet CDISC standards and regulator review, with QC and Pinnacle 21 checks, so correctness and auditability are hard even with modern LLM agents.

defensibility.rationale: Validated workflows inside sponsor environments and compliance trust could be sticky, but several funded AI clinical startups target adjacent work and CROs are incumbents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too recent to know; no acquisition or shutdown found as of 2026-11.

market_need_then: A source in search coverage says SDTM and ADaM mapping consumes up to 20 percent of statistical programming resources; AI clinical trial startups were raising seed rounds in 2026.

identity.voice_and_tone: positioned as AI for Clinical Trials and Statistical Programming, with expert review of every output

branding.community_and_virality: Gold sponsor of the BBSW 2026 statistics workshop, per its website.

brand_strength.rationale: Early stage; the name is a Greek mythology word shared with other organizations and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Astraea is a Spring 2026 company with Stanford founders automating regulated clinical trial programming. No funding or customers are public, the sector has several funded AI entrants, and trust in regulated outputs will decide whether sponsors adopt it, so the outcome is not yet knowable.
notes: One search summary reports a 130K seed tied to the YC batch and a May 2026 launch; this is a single source and unverified, so it is not recorded as a round. Dealroom shows an enterprise value range with no funding label. Search results listed team size as two while the YC page says six. Octozi, Cori Clinical and Clymb Clinical entered after the batch and are left out of the founding list. No news about shutdown or acquisition was found. The YC launch post URL was found in search results but the title appeared unrelated; the YC company page was used.
